**My thinking as this farmer:**

I have farmed this land for 30 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is not bad, and I have my well, so drought does not scare me as much as it scares others. My land is 10.7 mu — I rotate wheat and maize on the same fields every year, like everyone around here. Half for wheat in winter, same fields for maize in summer.

For wheat, I will sow in mid-October as I always do. I buy improved variety seed from the county seed shop — whatever the shop recommends that is popular with my neighbors. I am not experimenting at my age. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and urea when the plants joint in spring. I irrigate four times: the winter water before the ground freezes, then jointing, heading, and once during grain fill if it is dry. I spray twice — once for aphids, once for powdery mildew in spring.

For maize, I sow right after the wheat harvest in June, no rest. I use hybrid seed, I have used hybrid maize for over 20 years now —郑单958 type or whatever the seed shop has. I till lightly with the rotary machine before sowing wheat, but for maize I do not till deep, just rotary after wheat straw is handled. I apply urea in two splits — at sowing and at bell stage. I irrigate twice if rain is short. I spray once or twice for corn borer and fall armyworm.

I split the land evenly: 5.35 mu each.
